results.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai Pays a Courtesy Call on Nigerian First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu @SenRemiTinubu On October 22, 202
results.description:
Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai Pays a Courtesy Call on Nigerian First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu @SenRemiTinubu

On October 22, 2026, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai paid a courtesy call on H.E. Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON, First Lady of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Ambassador Yu stated that this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Nigeria. Over the past 55 years, the two countries have stood together through thick and thin, firmly supporting each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns. Under the strategic guidance of our two Heads of State, the China-Nigeria Comprehensive Strategic Partnership has entered a new stage of high-quality development. China is ready to work with Nigeria to strengthen practical cooperation across all sectors, accelerate the release of benefits from zero-tariff measures, and propel bilateral relations to new heights. Ambassador Yu also briefed her on the four principles for constructive participation by all parties in resolving African hotspot issues and four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation proposed by President Xi Jinping, emphasizing that China always respects Africa’s ownership and resource sovereignty, and looks forward to achieving win-win cooperation and common development with the continent.

Senator Oluremi Tinubu spoke highly of bilateral relations, thanking China for supporting Africa’s independent development through initiatives such as zero-tariff policies. She noted that China is a great partner of Nigeria, and the Nigerian side stands ready to make joint efforts with China to sustain the sound momentum of Nigeria-China relations.

results.description:
CBN seeks stronger banking ties, efficient cross-border payment system with China

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is seeking stronger banking ties and more efficient cross-border payment arrangements with China to facilitate financial transactions and investment between the two countries.

According to a statement on Thursday, Olayemi Cardoso, the CBN governor, made the call at a business and financial roundtable in Beijing on Wednesday, as Nigerian and Chinese business leaders discussed barriers to financial flows between both economies.

On October 22, 2026, Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Governor Olayemi Cardoso pushed for greater Chinese investment in Nigeria’s financial markets, including naira-denominated instruments.

The discussions involved the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC).

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

Nigeria already makes substantial trade-related payments to China, but investment flows into Nigeria remain comparatively limited.

Attracting Chinese financial institutions could help channel more foreign capital into Nigerian financial markets.

𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗧 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗡𝗦 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗜𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗦

More institutional participation could deepen market liquidity and create additional demand for Nigerian financial assets.

However, attracting foreign capital will depend on sustained economic stability, investor confidence and the ability to manage currency risks.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗤𝗨𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Can Nigeria turn its improving financial stability into actual investment inflows?

The discussions are a step towards that goal, but commitments, implementation and measurable capital inflows will matter more than announcements.
